issues.t: Rust, including front spring mounts that can tear away from the body
issues.sym: Rust bubbles around the wheel arches, door edges and trunk lock, or a loud bang and one front corner suddenly dropping.
issues.why: This generation is known for poor rust protection. The welded mount that holds the top of the front spring can corrode and separate from the inner fender.
issues.next: Have the front spring mounts inspected on a lift right away. If one is rusted or cracked, do not drive the car until it is repaired.

issues.t: Electronic brake system can drop into back-up mode (recall)
issues.sym: A red brake warning with a service brake message, and a pedal that suddenly needs much more effort and travel to stop the car.
issues.why: These cars use an electro-hydraulic brake system. A fault can switch it to a plain hydraulic back-up with no power assist.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 04V-296 and 05V-133. If the red brake warning appears, stop when safe and have the car towed.

issues.t: Electronic brake pump unit reaches the end of its service life
issues.sym: A brake service message that keeps returning, then a red warning and a hard pedal with weak braking.
issues.why: The brake pump unit counts brake applications and wears out after a set number. Mercedes-Benz USA extended warranty coverage on this unit to 25 years with no mileage limit.
issues.next: Ask a Mercedes dealer to replace the unit under the extended coverage. Do not keep driving with a red brake warning.

issues.t: Balance shaft or timing idler gear teeth wear down
issues.sym: Check engine light for camshaft timing, rough idle, misfires, hard starting and a growing rattle from the front of the engine.
issues.why: A gear on the balance shaft (V6) or the timing idler (V8) was made of metal that was too soft. As the teeth wear, valve timing drifts off. Later engines got a harder gear.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the engine serial number checked against the affected range. Do not keep driving with a timing rattle, since the chain can skip.

issues.t: Air suspension struts and compressor leak or fail
issues.sym: One corner or the whole car sitting low after parking, a car too low message, a compressor that runs constantly or a harsh, thumping ride.
issues.why: On cars with air suspension, the rubber in the air struts cracks with age and leaks. The compressor and valve block then wear out from running too much.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested soon. Do not drive on a fully collapsed corner, and fix leaks before they burn out the compressor.

issues.t: Diesel emissions settlement repair and extended warranty
issues.sym: Usually nothing to notice. Some owners see a check engine light or more frequent diesel exhaust fluid top-ups.
issues.why: Under a 2020 settlement with US regulators over emissions software, Mercedes-Benz agreed to update the software and some hardware on these diesels and extend the emissions warranty.
issues.next: Ask a Mercedes dealer whether the approved emissions modification has been done on your VIN and what the extended warranty covers.
src: EPA/CARB Clean Air Act settlement with Daimler (2020)

issues.t: Driveshaft joint can break on all-wheel-drive models (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration or clunking from under the car, or a sudden loss of drive while the engine still runs.
issues.why: A universal joint on the driveshaft of some 4MATIC cars can break.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-216 and have the driveshaft replaced free. Stop driving if you feel new driveline vibration.

issues.t: 48-volt battery fails and the car will not start
issues.sym: A 48V battery or stop vehicle message, then the car will not start or will not restart after a stop.
issues.why: The mild-hybrid system uses a separate 48-volt battery to start the engine. Owners and the auto press report that this battery or its electronics can fail early.
issues.next: Have a dealer test the 48-volt system and check for software updates and warranty coverage. Expect a tow if it will not start.

issues.t: Infotainment restart can blank the instrument display (recall)
issues.sym: The center screen reboots while driving and the speedometer and warning display go dark for a time.
issues.why: A software fault can make the infotainment computer reset, and the driver display goes blank with it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-281 and get the free software update. If the display goes blank, pull over when safe until it returns.

issues.t: Glass sunroof panel can come loose and fly off
issues.sym: Wind noise or a rattle from the roof, or the glass panel sits unevenly in its frame; in the worst case the panel leaves the car while driving.
issues.why: The bonding that holds the glass sunroof panel to its frame can weaken with age and heat, so the panel is no longer held securely.
issues.next: Have the sunroof inspected right away and leave it closed until a dealer confirms the panel is secure; the work is free under a safety recall.

issues.t: Power steering can lose its fluid (recall)
issues.sym: Steering turns heavy, a whine comes from the front of the car and reddish fluid shows up under the front end.
issues.why: A power steering line or connection can lose fluid, so the pump runs short and the help it gives the driver drops away.
issues.next: Stop driving if the steering goes heavy and have the car checked under the recall; losing assist at speed makes the car hard to control.

issues.t: Diesel fuel filter can leak
issues.sym: A strong diesel smell under the hood and wet, oily film or drips around the filter housing at the front of the engine.
issues.why: The fuel filter and its housing can seep at the seals, letting diesel escape under pressure.
issues.next: Have it replaced under the recall without waiting; leaking diesel on hot engine parts is a fire risk.

issues.t: Crankshaft vibration damper ring can separate (recall)
issues.sym: A knock or rumble from the front of the engine, or a loose metal ring found lying in the engine bay.
issues.why: Too little adhesive was used in build, so the inner mass ring of the vibration damper can come away from the pulley.
issues.next: Have the damper inspected and replaced under the recall; a loose ring can wreck the belt drive and hurt someone working under the hood.

issues.t: Harsh or jerky automatic gear changes
issues.sym: A thump or jerk shifting from first to second and second to third, and the gearbox can feel like it hunts before it settles.
issues.why: The shift software and the torque converter lock-up clutch can work against each other, and aged fluid or a worn valve body makes it worse.
issues.next: Have the fluid level and the transmission software checked at the next service; it is safe to keep driving, but shift quality only gets worse if it is left.

issues.t: Oil can leak from the timing chain tensioner gasket (recall)
issues.sym: A burning oil smell, oil drips at the front of the engine and an oil level that falls between changes.
issues.why: The gasket at the chain tensioner can seep, and the oil it lets out runs onto hot parts of the engine.
issues.next: Have the gasket replaced under the recall without delay; oil on a hot engine can catch fire.

issues.t: Diesel oil cooler seals leak oil into the engine valley
issues.sym: Low oil warnings, an oil smell through the vents and oil pooling at the back of the engine and around the bell housing.
issues.why: The oil cooler sits in the V of the engine, and its rubber seals harden with heat until they no longer hold oil in.
issues.next: Have the seals replaced before the level gets low; the intake has to come off for the job, so a small leak is cheaper to fix than a big one.

issues.t: Rattle from the engine for a few seconds on a cold start
issues.sym: A rattle or chatter for a second or two after a cold start, sometimes with a slow crank and a check engine light for cam timing.
issues.why: The camshaft adjusters bleed down overnight and the secondary chain tensioners have no oil pressure until the engine builds it, so the chain slaps.
issues.next: Have the cam timing codes read at the next service; a rattle that lasts longer as the months pass needs attention before the chain guides wear.

issues.t: Transmission wiring connection can corrode and short (recall)
issues.sym: A hot plastic smell, transmission warning messages or the car dropping into a limited limp-home mode.
issues.why: The transmission wiring connection was put together wrongly, so moisture gets in, corrodes the pins and can short across them.
issues.next: Have it corrected under the recall right away; a short in this harness can start a fire.

issues.t: Tires marked with the wrong maximum pressure (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing shows while driving; the pressure number moulded into the tire sidewall is higher than the tire is actually built for.
issues.why: The tires were marked with a maximum inflation pressure they do not meet, so anyone filling to the sidewall number overinflates them.
issues.next: Have the tires replaced under the recall, and in the meantime set pressures to the door sticker rather than the sidewall; an overinflated tire can fail.

issues.t: Loose battery ground connections can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A hot electrical smell, odd electrical faults around the car or an engine that will not start.
issues.why: The 12-volt and 48-volt ground connections may not have been tightened properly in build, so they heat up when current runs through them.
issues.next: Have the grounds checked and tightened under the recall promptly; a hot connection can start a fire.

issues.t: Rear camber strut bracket can break away from the axle carrier (recall)
issues.sym: The back of the car feels loose or wanders in a straight line, often with a clunk from the rear over bumps.
issues.why: The bracket that holds the rear camber strut may have been welded badly and can separate from the rear axle carrier.
issues.next: Do not drive the car until a dealer has inspected it under the recall; if the bracket lets go the rear wheel can steer on its own.

issues.t: Cross-traffic automatic braking can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The car no longer brakes by itself when something crosses behind while reversing, usually with no warning message.
issues.why: A software fault in the infotainment system switches off the braking part of the cross-traffic alert.
issues.next: Have the software updated under the recall and keep looking behind you yourself when backing out.
